prose.intro_html: Stroganoff has a reputation as fussy Sunday food, but the ground beef version is a Tuesday and always was. You brown the beef, build a quick pan sauce out of mushrooms, a little brandy, and sour cream, and you are done in about half an hour. The only trick for keeping it low carb is what goes underneath. Instead of egg noodles, this one rides on cabbage cut into thin strips and fried soft in the pan, so it eats like noodles without the carbs. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 15 grams of carbs. That is comfort food that does not fight your macros or your wallet.
shop_smart: Three and a half pounds of lean ground beef is the anchor. Reach for the 93/7 so the sauce does not turn greasy, and buy the big family pack instead of the little trays so you are paying for beef, not packaging. This is where most of the money and all of the protein live.

A pound of cabbage per few servings is the noodle. You want about two and a half pounds of green cabbage, roughly one and a third heads, sliced into thin strips and fried until tender. If you would rather, riced cauliflower is the classic low-carb swap and goes in one for one; the recipe is built on cabbage because it is cheaper and it is on the shelf.

Fourteen ounces of white mushrooms and one onion carry the flavor. Sliced mushrooms browned in butter give the sauce its body, and a little chopped onion rounds it out. Both are cheap staples that stretch across everything else you cook.

Full-fat sour cream and cream cheese make it creamy. Buy the real full-fat sour cream and a block of cream cheese rather than the light versions, because the fat is what keeps the sauce smooth and rich instead of thin. Together they are the whole point of stroganoff.

Butter, brandy, Worcestershire, beef base, nutmeg, and parsley are the seasoning. The brandy deglazes the pan and the beef base and Worcestershire deepen the sauce; a pinch of nutmeg and a little fresh parsley finish it. These are backbone items you buy once and cook with for a long time.
make_it: Weigh your empty pot or the biggest skillet you own and write the number down. You will use it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight instead of eyeballing every container.
Slice the mushrooms, chop the onion, and chop the parsley. Cut the cabbage into thin strips so it cooks down like noodles.
Set a large skillet over medium heat and fry the cabbage strips until tender, about 8 to 10 minutes. Move the cooked cabbage to a bowl and keep it warm while you build the sauce.

In the same skillet, melt most of the butter and brown the mushrooms without crowding them, about 4 minutes, then push them to the side and saute the onion in the rest of the butter until soft. Scoop the mushrooms and onion out and set them aside, then brown the ground beef in the pan, breaking it into small pieces until just cooked through.
Pour in the brandy, stir in the beef base and the Worcestershire, and scrape the browned bits up off the bottom of the pan.

Return the mushrooms and onion and any juices to the pan, sprinkle over the nutmeg, and let the liquid simmer down for a minute. Stir in the cream cheese until it melts, then stir in the sour cream and simmer gently until the sauce thickens. Stir in the parsley and season to taste.
Fold the cooked cabbage back into the sauce so every strand is coated, then weigh the pot and portion as below.
prose.portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the cooked total. Divide that number by 14 and spoon that exact weight into each container. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

head.description: Low carb ground beef stroganoff for meal prep: browned lean beef in a creamy mushroom and sour cream sauce served over fried cabbage noodles, built for 14 servings. About {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, with under 15 grams of carbs.
head.keywords: ground beef stroganoff, low carb stroganoff, cabbage noodles, low carb meal prep, high protein beef dinner
steps: Slice the mushrooms and cabbage, and chop the onion and parsley.
Fry the cabbage strips until tender, then set aside and keep warm.
Brown the mushrooms and onion in butter, remove them, then brown the ground beef.
Add the brandy, beef base, and Worcestershire and scrape up the browned bits.
Return the mushrooms and onion with the nutmeg, melt in the cream cheese, stir in the sour cream, and simmer until thick, then stir in the parsley.
Fold the cabbage back in, weigh the pot, subtract the empty weight, and divide across 14 containers.
